newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's DAX higher, traders look to year-end.
newsitem.headline: Germany's DAX higher, traders look to year-end.

text.p: German shares were up over half a percent in low-volume afternoon post-bourse trade, lifted mainly by the ongoing strength of the dollar. Most market players are still on Christmas holiday, dealers said.

They added that next week should be busier, as many traders were preparing themselves for the year-end. There was also very little data of any significance to drive the market to any new significant highs.
At 1437 GMT the IBIS DAX index stood at 2,859.38 points, up 15.29 points, or 0.54 percent. The dollar stood at 1.5557/62 to the mark.
Shares in the news included Daimler-Benz, which was up 1.50 marks at 103.70 marks after its Mercedes carmaker unit released upbeat figures and positive forecasts for 1997.
Viag AG was higher after the announcement that the diversified utility held 10.26 percent of Bayerische Vereinsbank.
Deutsche Bank recovered from earlier losses to trade up 1.13 marks at 71.72 marks.
